name: ADP5063ACPZ-1-R7
title: Linear single-cell LiFePO4 charger with power path, I2C control and USB current limits, 4 mm × 4 mm LFCSP
summary: The ADP5063 is a linear charger for one LiFePO4 or Li-Ion cell with an internal power path: an LDO feeds the system rail from USB or an adapter while a separate FET links the rail to the battery, so the system runs even with a dead or absent cell. It takes 4 V to 6.7 V and withstands 20 V, gives up to 2.1 A to the system and up to 1.3 A into the cell, and sets input limits for USB 2.0, USB 3.0 and dedicated chargers. Every threshold and current is set over I2C, three factory-assigned DIG_IO pins give direct control, and a pack thermistor input supports JEITA. The -1 version ends charge at 3.60 V by default.
key_figures: 4 V to 6.7 V operating, −0.5 V to +20 V tolerated

rows: Charger; defaults VTRM 3.60 V, ICHG 750 mA, IEND 52.5 mA, VSYSTEM 4.3 V, 10 kΩ NTC beta 3150, DIG_IOx option 0101

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: USB VBUS or an adapter feeds VINx through a 10 µF input capacitor. The system rail comes off ISO_Sx with 22 µF; the cell sits on ISO_Bx with BAT_SNS tied to the same node and 22 µF across it. A thermistor from THR to ground watches the pack temperature, ILED sinks current through an LED and resistor from VLED, and the I2C lines, the three DIG_IO controls and the SYS_EN flag go to the host.

notes: The DIG_IO pins' functions are set at the factory.

circuits.title: Reference circuit
circuits.description: The full hookup with part numbers: 4 V to 7 V on VIN1 to VIN3 with a 10 µF 25 V capacitor, 100 nF on CBP, 22 µF on the ISO_S pins for the system and 22 µF on the battery node. BAT_SNS joins ISO_B1 to ISO_B3 at the battery positive terminal. 1.5 kΩ pull-ups to VDDIO serve SCL and SDA, 10 kΩ pulls SYS_EN up to VDDIO for the MCU, an optional 10 kΩ NTC in the pack goes from THR to ground, and the LED on ILED runs from VLED through a resistor.

operation.text: The charger runs from 4 V to 6.7 V on VINx and survives up to 20 V there, so spikes on USB VBUS when a cable goes in or out do no harm. Above VVIN_OV (6.9 V typical) the input is blocked. Until VINx reaches VIN_OK with no proper battery voltage present, the blocking stage draws under 1 mA.

An internal FET joins the charger output (ISO_Sx, the system rail) to the battery (ISO_Bx). With it the system runs at once from USB even when the battery is dead or missing. The LDO puts out up to 2.1 A at an I2C-set 4.3 V to 5.0 V, and charge current into the cell goes up to 1.3 A from a dedicated charger.

VINx current is limited by ILIM[3:0], 100 mA by default so that an unconfigured USB host or hub is respected. On this part DIG_IO1 high selects 500 mA and DIG_IO2 high selects 1500 mA. Writing ILIM over I2C overrides the pins. When the limit leaves less current than ICHG asks for, charging slows and VIN_ILIM is set. An external USB detection chip tells the system which source is attached so the right limit can be set.

A cell below VTRK_DEAD (2.0 V default) gets ITRK_DEAD (20 mA default), which can reset a pack protection circuit and bring the cell up safely. The LDO holds ISO_Sx at VISO_STRK and the isolation FET is off, so the battery is cut off from the system. If the cell has not reached VTRK_DEAD after 60 minutes, charging stops with a fault in CHARGER_STATUS.

Between VTRK_DEAD and VWEAK the battery is too low to run the whole system, so the USB transceiver cannot ask the host for more current and the limit stays at 100 mA. At least 20 mA goes to the cell through the trickle branch, keeping a microcontroller on ISO_Sx alive; any current the system leaves over also charges the cell. The isolation FET holds ISO_Sx at VISO_SFC. Isothermal control or the input limit can keep the current below its setting.

Above VWEAK the cell charges at ICHG and CHARGER_STATUS reads 010. Isothermal control or the input limit can hold the current lower. When the battery is below VISO_SFC the isolation FET keeps ISO_Sx at VISO_SFC.
When BAT_SNS reaches VTRM the charger holds VTRM there and lets the current fall, so the series resistance of the pack and board does not cut the charge short. CHARGER_STATUS reads 011.

If BAT_SNS has not reached VTRM within tCHG, charging stops with a fault. If VTRM was reached but the current is still above IEND when tCHG ends, charging stops without a fault and starts again normally at the recharge threshold.

The watchdog starts when the processor first sets RESET_WD or when the battery passes VWEAK, and from then must be reset within tWD. If it runs out during charging the safety timer tSAFE starts, ILIM returns to its default if parameters had been programmed, charging goes on for tSAFE, and then the charger turns off and sets CHARGER_STATUS.

In constant voltage mode, current below IEND for tEND ends charging and sets CHDONE; a dip shorter than tEND restarts the timer. Afterwards the charger watches BAT_SNS and restarts at VRCH, normally straight into constant voltage. Recharge can be turned off over I2C; register 0x0C bit 3 then flags that a recharge is due.

DIS_IC1 (I2C, or DIG_IO2 where so programmed) turns off all internal control and can also set the LDO and isolation FET states. In that mode VINx reaches the internal supply directly, so VINx must stay within VISO_Bx < VINx < 5.5 V.
EN_CHG low over I2C stops charging while the LDO keeps supplying the system at its set voltage. On this part DIG_IO3 also switches charging; a write to EN_CHG overrides the pin.

With EN_CHG_VLIM set (register 0x08 bit 5, off by default), charging enabled by EN_CHG or DIG_IO3 does not begin while the battery is above VCHG_VLIM (3.2 V typical). Once the battery drops below it, a full cycle runs to VTRM (3.6 V typical). Skipping top-ups of a half-full cell can lengthen cell life.
SYS_EN is an open-drain flag that can hold the system off until the battery can support start-up. Its behaviour is chosen by SYS_EN_SET (four modes, default set at the factory).

The open-drain ILED pin drives an LED or serves a microcontroller as a status line: on continuously while charging, blinking 167 ms on and 833 ms off after a timer fault, 1 sec on and 1 sec off in thermal shutdown, off otherwise.

Above TLIM (115°C typical) die temperature, charge current is cut back to hold the die there and returns as it cools; THERM_LIM is set meanwhile. Charge current can therefore be set for typical rather than worst-case conditions. There is no such loop on the ISO_Sx load in LDO mode: above 130°C an interrupt is raised and above 140°C the part shuts down.

Above TSD the charger turns off and sets TSD 140°C. It can run again once the die is below the falling threshold and the bit is cleared by writing register 0x0D bit 0 or cycling power. Above TSDL an early warning bit is set first, so the system can shed load.
With CHARGER_STATUS = 110, remove the cause, then cycle VINx power or write 1 to the fault bits in register 0x0D.

Below VVIN_OK_RISE on VINx the FET is fully on. It is off in trickle charge. Above VTRK_DEAD it regulates ISO_Sx at VISO_SFC, and once the battery passes VISO_SFC it is fully on. When ISO_Sx falls below ISO_Bx under heavy load it turns fully on so the battery helps supply the system (ideal diode); when ISO_Sx rises above ISO_Bx again it regulates or conducts according to the cell voltage and charger mode.

The charger first sinks ISINK from ISO_Bx for tBATOK: above VBATL at the end means a battery is present and charging begins; otherwise it sources ISOURCE for tBATOK. Reaching VBATH in that time means no battery; staying below means a battery is present.

A short comes from a damaged cell or a tripped pack protector. If ISO_Bx or BAT_SNS stays below VBATH after the source phase, trickle charge starts. If BAT_SNS is still below VBAT_SHR after tBAT_SHR, a short is declared: the isolation FET opens while the LDO keeps the system at VISO_STRK, and trickle current continues until the 60 minute trickle timer ends.

THR drives a current pulse into the pack NTC every 167 ms and stops charging below 0°C or above 60°C. The thermistor is 10 kΩ or 100 kΩ at 25°C (10 kΩ on this part) with one of eight beta values from 3150 to 4400 (3150 on this part). Without a pack thermistor a 10 kΩ ±20% resistor from THR to AGND is needed; an open THR reads as below 0°C and blocks charging. EN_THR defaults to 0.

JEITA1 or JEITA2 is turned on and chosen over I2C, or made the default at the factory. In the cool band JEITA1 halves the charge current while JEITA2 lowers VTRM by 100 mV; both lower VTRM by 100 mV when warm. In the cold or hot band charging stops and the isolation FET stays on so the part carries on in LDO mode.

The chip address is 0x28 for writes and 0x29 for reads; fast mode to 400 kHz. A write sends the address, a subaddress and data; the subaddress steps up after each byte until a stop. A read sets the subaddress with a write, then a repeated start with the read address returns data from successive registers until the master stops. Registers return to defaults when VINx falls below VVIN_OK_FALL, and when the battery is removed with VIN at 0 V.

The effective capacitance on ISO_Sx, counting the system's own capacitors, must stay between 10 µF and 100 µF at all times, after DC bias, temperature and tolerance. X5R or X7R rated 6.3 V or more suits; Y5V and Z5U do not. When the capacitance is split among loads, at least 5 µF sits at the ISO_Sx pins.
ISO_Bx and ISO_Sx each need at least 10 µF effective at all times; 22 µF nominal usually achieves it.
CBP decouples the internal supply. Keep it at or below 140 nF, and connect nothing else to the pin: no source and no load.

USB 2.0 asks that VBUS capacitance on a peripheral be 1 µF to 10 µF. If VINx may see up to 20 V, the capacitor must be rated above 20 V, which usually means a larger case; with a lower guaranteed maximum a smaller part will do.

The reference floor plan puts C1 (100 nF, 16 V X7R, 0402) beside the CBP pin with its ground on PGND, C4 (10 µF, 25 V X5R, 0805) between the VINx copper and PGND, C3 (22 µF, 16 V X5R, 1206) between the ISO_Sx copper and PGND, and C2 (22 µF, 16 V X5R, 1206) between the ISO_Bx copper and PGND, each next to its pins. BAT_SNS connects close to the battery positive terminal.

θJA is for a JEDEC 4-layer board; real boards differ, so maximise copper, preferably on outer layers. Shutdown is at 140°C; normal running resumes below 110°C once the TSD 140°C bit is cleared over I2C. Measuring input and output power at worst case gives the dissipation directly.

Defaults for termination voltage, charge current, end of charge current, trickle threshold, system voltage, thermistor value and beta, DIS_IC1 behaviour, timer fault action, SYS_EN mode, DIG_IO1 polarity and the DIG_IOx functions are set at the factory. Other combinations are available on request.
